prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer faces downward toward their own torso and a vertical metal grid fence directly in front of them, with no other people present in the scene. The wearer's raised left arm and hand gripping the upper bars are brightest and closest to the camera (roughly 0.2 to 0.4 m away above and to the left), while their torso below (0.3 to 0.5 m), their right hand holding a thin metal tool or blade against the lower bars (0.5 to 0.7 m below and to the right), and the grid plane receding downward toward the concrete base (~1.0 to 1.5 m) are progressively darker and within arm's reach. Across the five frames, the left arm shifts slightly leftward while the right hand moves the tool steadily back and forth along the lower grid bar, with the left forearm occluding the upper-left section of the fence and the wearer's lower body remaining out of view below the bottom edge. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground limbs and the thin metal grid bars from the background, though it is unreliable for the sunlit dirt ground visible through the open grid squares, which is rendered uniformly black at infinite or unresolved depth rather than at its actual ~1.5 m distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's visible body parts—their raised left arm, lower torso, and lowered right arm holding a tool—in the foreground (within 0.2 to 0.7 m) against an unsegmented black background representing the metal grid fence and ground in front of and below them. Both arms and the tool are within the wearer's immediate reach, separated from each other by roughly 0.3 to 0.5 m across the frame as the right hand slides slightly along the lower fence bar across the five frames while the wearer continues looking straight down. While the map helps group the wearer's self-occluding limbs and shirt into foreground regions distinct from the cluttered sunlit background and shadow patterns in RGB, it completely omits the metal grid fence, concrete ledge, and hand-held tool as separate object classes. Furthermore, the map is highly unreliable in its instance splitting and classification: in frame 1 it mislabels the upper-left corner and main body mask as 'horse', and in frames 3 through 5 it fragments the single camera wearer into two separate 'person' instances (splitting the left arm from the torso and right arm).
descriptions.pose: The pose map sits on a black background and detects only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-central foreground (roughly 0.5 to 0.7 m below the camera and 0.3 to 0.4 m below and to the right of the raised left arm), confirming no other people are facing or looking toward the wearer. In frames 1, 2, and 5, this skeleton shows the right wrist extending from the bottom edge with the thumb and index finger pointed forward and upward toward the metal grid bar within arm's reach, shifting slightly upward between frames 1 and 2 as the hand advances along the bar. This map makes the fine finger articulation and grip orientation of the right hand clearer than in the shadowed RGB view, where the dark metal tool partially blends with the fence. However, the pose map is largely unreliable across the sequence: it completely misses the wearer's yellow body skeleton in all frames, fails to detect the close-up left hand gripping the top of the frame (which is partly cropped at the upper boundary), and drops the right hand detection entirely in frames 3 and 4.
